chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Mabindath narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Hilal narrated to us, from Abu Malik al-Hadhrami, from Abu as-Safatij, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to them (to Abu Abdullah or to Abu Ja'far): Can this matter (imamate) be entrusted to one who has not yet reached adulthood? He said: It will be so. I said: What does he do? He said: He is granted knowledge and wisdom, and he is not left to his own self (fancies).

key_terms.وَلَا يَكِلُهُ إِلَى نَفْسِهِ: and he is not left to his own self (fancies/inclinations)

ai.seo_question: Can the Imam be a child or young person who has not reached adulthood?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* confirms the Shia doctrine of the Imamate of a child, specifically referencing the future al-Qa'im, where divine authority is not contingent upon physical maturity. The Imam explains that such a figure is endowed with innate 'ilm (knowledge) and preserved from error by being 'not left to himself,' ensuring his guidance remains pure despite his young age. This underscores the concept of 'ismah (infallibility) extending to the period of childhood, distinguishing the Imam from ordinary humans who require gradual intellectual development.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (2) Muhammad bin Hammam narrated from Ahmad bin Mabindath from Ahmad bin Hilal from Abu Malik al-Hadhrami from Abu as-Safatij that Abu Baseer had said:

“I said to one of them-Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) or Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as): “Can this matter (imamate) be entrusted to one, who is not adult yet?” He said: “It will be so.” I said: “How does he (the young imam) act?” He said: “Allah grants him with knowledge and wisdom and does not make him follow his fancies.”
